nodes.summary: Minus[x] is the arithmetic negation of x, equivalent to -x (Times[-1, x]).

nodes.label: MixedGraphQ
nodes.summary: MixedGraphQ[g] gives True if g has both directed and undirected edges.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.summary: Module[{x, y, ...}, expr] specifies that x, y, ... are local variables.

nodes.label: Modulus
nodes.summary: Modulus is an option for Solve.  Solve[poly == 0, x, Modulus -> p]

nodes.label: MoebiusMu
nodes.summary: MoebiusMu[n] gives the Moebius function mu(n): 0 if n has a squared prime factor, otherwise (-1)^k where k is the number of distinct primes. A non-real Gaussian-integer argument is handled over Z[i].

nodes.label: MonomialList
nodes.summary: MonomialList[poly] gives the list of monomials of poly, using Variables[poly].

nodes.label: MorphologicalComponents
nodes.summary: MorphologicalComponents[image] labels the connected components of the foreground, giving an INTEGER MATRIX with background 0 and components numbered 1..k in raster order of first appearance. MorphologicalComponents[image, t] takes pixels above t as foreground (default 0, so nonzero is foreground). CornerNeighbors -> False uses 4-connectivity instead of the default 8. Two pixels touching only at a corner are ONE component under 8 and TWO under 4, which is the property that distinguishes the two rules -- every other property holds under either. A matrix rather than an Image, deliberately: Image type inference would call a label array of 1..12 a "Byte" image and ImageData would then divide every label by 255. Labels are indices, not brightnesses. Contiguous labels in scan order mean Max of the result is the component count.

nodes.label: Most
nodes.summary: Most[expr] gives all but the last element of expr.

nodes.label: MultiplicativeOrder
nodes.summary: MultiplicativeOrder[k, n] gives the multiplicative order of k modulo n, the smallest positive integer m such that k^m is congruent to 1 modulo n; reversing it -- recovering the exponent x with k^x congruent to a given target -- is the discrete logarithm problem, whose presumed hardness underlies Diffie-Hellman key exchange and the ElGamal and DSA schemes.

nodes.label: Names
nodes.summary: Names["string"] gives a sorted list of the names of symbols matching the string. Names[patt] matches a string pattern with metacharacters * (zero or more characters) and @ (one or more non-uppercase characters), or a RegularExpression["re"]. Names[{p1, p2, ...}] matches any of the patterns. Names[] lists all symbol names.

nodes.label: NeighborhoodGraph
nodes.summary: NeighborhoodGraph[g, v] gives the subgraph of g induced by v and its neighbours; NeighborhoodGraph[g, v, k] by the vertices within distance k of v (k a non-negative integer or Infinity), edge direction ignored. NeighborhoodGraph[g, {v1, ...}, k] uses several centres. Vertices: the centres, then each centre's new vertices in VertexList order.

nodes.label: NextPrime
nodes.summary: NextPrime[x] gives the next prime after x.

nodes.label: NormalDistribution
nodes.summary: NormalDistribution[mu, sigma] represents a normal distribution; NormalDistribution[] is the standard normal. Unlike a fitted model it prints its parameters in full, because they are what the user specified rather than an implementation detail.

nodes.label: NumberForm
nodes.summary: NumberForm[expr, n] prints approximate real numbers in expr to n-digit

nodes.label: NumericQ
nodes.summary: NumericQ[expr] gives True if expr is a numeric quantity, and False otherwise.

nodes.label: OddQ
nodes.summary: OddQ[n] gives True if n is an odd integer (Integer or BigInt), False otherwise.

nodes.label: OneIdentity
nodes.summary: OneIdentity is an attribute that can be assigned to a symbol f to indicate that f[x], f[f[x]], etc. are all equivalent to x for the purpose of pattern matching.

nodes.label: Opening
nodes.summary: Opening[image, r] erodes then dilates with the same element, removing bright features smaller than it while leaving larger ones close to their original size. IDEMPOTENT: Opening[Opening[f]] equals Opening[f], which is the defining property and the reason opening twice is not a sharpening loop.

nodes.label: OptionValue
nodes.summary: OptionValue[name] gives the value of an option named name in the

nodes.label: Options
nodes.summary: Options[f] gives the list of default option rules for the symbol f.

nodes.label: Order
nodes.summary: Order[e1, e2] gives 1 if e1 is before e2 in canonical order, -1 if e1 is after e2, and 0 if e1 is identical to e2.

nodes.label: OrderedQ
nodes.summary: OrderedQ[h[e1, e2, ...]] gives True if the elements are in canonical order, and False otherwise.

nodes.label: Ordering
nodes.summary: Ordering[list] gives the positions in list at which each successive element of Sort[list] appears, so that list[[Ordering[list]]] is Sort[list].

nodes.label: Orderless
nodes.summary: Orderless is an attribute that can be assigned to a symbol f to indicate that the elements e_i in expressions of the form f[e_1, e_2, ...] should automatically be sorted into canonical order. This property is accounted for in pattern matching.

nodes.label: OrderlessPatternSequence
nodes.summary: OrderlessPatternSequence[p1, p2, ...] is a pattern object that matches a sequence of arguments, in any order, that together match p1, p2, ....

nodes.label: OwnValues
nodes.summary: OwnValues[s] gives a list of own-value rules for s.

nodes.label: PDEClassify
nodes.summary: PDEClassify[eqn, u, {v1, v2}] classifies a second-order linear PDE by the discriminant Δ = B² − 4 A C of its principal part A u_{v1 v1} + B u_{v1 v2} + C u_{v2 v2}: "Hyperbolic" (Δ > 0, e.g. the wave equation), "Parabolic" (Δ == 0, e.g. the heat equation), or "Elliptic" (Δ < 0, e.g. Laplace's equation). Only the highest-order terms determine the type. A discriminant whose sign is not a decidable constant (a mixed-type / parameter-dependent equation such as Tricomi's y u_xx + u_yy == 0) leaves the call unevaluated.

nodes.label: PDF
nodes.summary: PDF[dist, x] gives the probability density of dist at x, and threads over a list of x. Supports NormalDistribution and UniformDistribution.

nodes.label: PageRankCentrality
nodes.summary: PageRankCentrality[g, a] gives the PageRank of each vertex with damping factor a (default 0.85): x = a P^T x + (1-a)/n, where a vertex with no outgoing edge links to every vertex; the entries sum to 1. Edge weights are ignored.

nodes.label: ParametricPlot3D
nodes.summary: ParametricPlot3D[{fx, fy, fz}, {t, tmin, tmax}, opts...]

nodes.label: PartitionsP
nodes.summary: PartitionsP[n] gives the number p(n) of unrestricted partitions of the integer n, evaluated exactly through the Hardy-Ramanujan-Rademacher series (p(n) grows like exp(Pi Sqrt[2n/3])).

nodes.label: PartitionsQ
nodes.summary: PartitionsQ[n] gives the number q(n) of partitions of the integer n into distinct parts -- equal, by Euler's theorem, to the number of partitions into odd parts.

nodes.label: PathGraph
nodes.summary: PathGraph[n] gives the path on n vertices; PathGraph[{v1,...}] the path over the given vertices.

nodes.label: PathGraphQ
nodes.summary: PathGraphQ[g] gives True if g is a path: connected with at least one vertex and, if undirected, every degree at most 2 and one edge fewer than vertices; if directed, every in- and out-degree at most 1. Mixed graphs are never paths.

nodes.label: PatternSequence
nodes.summary: PatternSequence[p1, p2, ...] is a pattern object that matches a sequence of arguments, each in turn matching p1, p2, ....

nodes.label: Pause
nodes.summary: Pause[n] pauses for at least n seconds.

nodes.label: Perimeter
nodes.summary: Perimeter[Polygon[{{x1, y1}, ...}]] gives the perimeter of a simple 2D polygon: the sum of its edge lengths, including the closing edge. Exact coordinates give an exact (possibly symbolic, e.g. 2 + Sqrt[2]) result; Real coordinates give a machine-precision result.

nodes.label: PetersenGraph
nodes.summary: PetersenGraph[] gives the Petersen graph; PetersenGraph[n, k] the generalized Petersen graph: inner vertices 1..n with i joined to i+k (mod n), outer cycle n+1..2n, and spokes i to n+i.

nodes.label: PlanarGraphQ
nodes.summary: PlanarGraphQ[g] gives True if g can be drawn in the plane without edge crossings. Linear-time left-right planarity test; gives False for non-graphs.

nodes.label: Plot3D
nodes.summary: Plot3D[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts...]

nodes.label: Plus
nodes.summary: x + y + ... or Plus[x, y, ...] represents a sum of terms.

nodes.label: PolynomialExtendedGCD
nodes.summary: PolynomialExtendedGCD[poly1, poly2, x] gives the extended GCD of poly1 and poly2 treated as univariate polynomials in x.

nodes.label: PolynomialGCD
nodes.summary: PolynomialGCD[poly1, poly2, ...] gives the greatest common divisor of the polynomials.

nodes.label: PolynomialLCM
nodes.summary: PolynomialLCM[poly1, poly2, ...] gives the least common multiple of the polynomials.

nodes.label: PolynomialQuotient
nodes.summary: PolynomialQuotient[p, q, x] gives the quotient of p and q, treated as polynomials in x, with any remainder dropped.

nodes.label: PolynomialReduce
nodes.summary: PolynomialReduce[poly, {p1, ..., pn}, {x1, ..., xk}] gives {{a1, ..., an}, b} with

nodes.label: PolynomialRemainder
nodes.summary: PolynomialRemainder[p, q, x] gives the remainder from dividing p by q, treated as polynomials in x.

nodes.label: PolynomialSqrt
nodes.summary: PolynomialSqrt[p] gives a polynomial s with s^2 == p when p is a perfect square (every non-constant irreducible factor has even multiplicity; the numeric content is carried through Sqrt), and $Failed otherwise. PolynomialSqrt[p, x] treats p as a polynomial in x.

nodes.label: Position
nodes.summary: Position[expr, pattern] gives a list of the positions at which objects matching pattern appear in expr.

nodes.label: PossibleZeroQ
nodes.summary: PossibleZeroQ[expr] gives True if symbolic and numerical methods suggest that expr has value zero, and False otherwise.

nodes.label: Power
nodes.summary: x ^ y or Power[x, y] represents x to the power y.

nodes.label: PowerMod
nodes.summary: PowerMod[a, b, m] gives a^b mod m by square-and-multiply, reducing modulo m at every step so the full power is never formed.

nodes.label: Predict
nodes.summary: Predict[data] fits a predictor to data and returns a PredictorFunction, which can be stored and applied to new inputs. Data is either a list of rules {features -> value, ...} or a matrix whose last column is the response. Method -> "LinearRegression" is the only method implemented and is the default; any other declines rather than silently linear-regressing. The returned object also answers "Method", "Coefficients" and "FeatureCount". A collinear feature set has no unique fit and returns unevaluated.

nodes.label: PredictorFunction
nodes.summary: PredictorFunction[method, coefficients, featureCount] is the fitted object Predict returns. Apply it to a feature vector to get a prediction, or to "Method", "Coefficients" or "FeatureCount" to read it. A one-feature model also accepts a bare scalar.

nodes.label: Prepend
nodes.summary: Prepend[expr, elem] adds elem to the beginning of expr.

nodes.label: Prime
nodes.summary: Prime[n] gives the nth prime number. Listable. Small n is read from a sieve table; large n inverts PrimePi via an asymptotic estimate refined against the exact prime counter. Defined for positive integers up to n ~ 1.4*10^12; non-positive-integer arguments give Prime::intpp.

nodes.label: PrimeNu
nodes.summary: PrimeNu[n] gives the number of distinct prime factors of n, nu(n). PrimeNu[n, GaussianIntegers -> True] (or a non-real Gaussian-integer n) counts distinct Gaussian prime factors over Z[i]. PrimeNu[1] is 0; PrimeNu[0] is left unevaluated.

nodes.label: PrimeOmega
nodes.summary: PrimeOmega[n] gives the number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity, Omega(n). PrimeOmega[n, GaussianIntegers -> True] (or a non-real Gaussian-integer n) counts Gaussian prime factors over Z[i]. PrimeOmega[1] is 0; PrimeOmega[0] is left unevaluated.

nodes.label: PrimePi
nodes.summary: PrimePi[x] gives the number of primes less than or equal to x, exact for x up to 5*10^13 (larger x is left unevaluated). The option Method -> m selects the algorithm: Automatic (default), "Sieve", "Legendre", "Meissel", "Lehmer", "LMO" (Lagarias-Miller-Odlyzko), "DelegliseRivat", or "LucyHedgehog".

nodes.label: PrimeQ
nodes.summary: PrimeQ[n] gives True if n is a prime integer and False otherwise, using a Baillie-PSW and Miller-Rabin probabilistic primality test (no known counterexample, and definite below 2^64).

nodes.label: PrimitiveRoot
nodes.summary: PrimitiveRoot[n] gives the smallest primitive root of n -- a generator of the multiplicative group (Z/nZ)* of units modulo n.

nodes.label: PrimitiveRootList
nodes.summary: PrimitiveRootList[n] gives the sorted list of all primitive roots of n in the canonical residues {1, ..., n-1}; when n admits any, there are exactly EulerPhi[EulerPhi[n]] of them.

nodes.label: PrincipalComponents
nodes.summary: PrincipalComponents[matrix] gives the rows of matrix in principal-component coordinates, components ordered by decreasing variance. Rows are observations and columns are variables. Method -> "Correlation" standardises each variable to unit variance first, which is what you want when the columns have different units; the default "Covariance" does not.

nodes.label: Pruning
nodes.summary: Pruning[image] removes one pixel from every free end of the foreground; Pruning[image, n] repeats that n times, which shortens each branch by up to n and deletes any branch shorter than that. Used after Thinning to remove the short spurs a skeleton grows at boundary irregularities. An end point has exactly one foreground neighbour, so an ISOLATED pixel is not one and survives: pruning shortens branches rather than erasing specks. Pruning[image, 0] is the image unchanged. The result is a "Bit" image.

nodes.label: Quartics
nodes.summary: Quartics is an option for Solve that controls whether quartic

nodes.label: Quiet
nodes.summary: Quiet[expr] evaluates expr with messages suppressed and returns its value. Quiet[expr, spec] suppresses all messages regardless of spec.

nodes.label: RandomGraph
nodes.summary: RandomGraph[{n, m}] gives a random undirected graph with n vertices and m edges. RandomGraph[{n, m}, k] gives a list of k such graphs; memory use grows with k.

nodes.label: RandomHypergraph
nodes.summary: RandomHypergraph[{n, m}, k] gives a k-uniform hypergraph on 1..n with m independent uniformly random k-subsets as hyperedges; RandomHypergraph[{n, m}, k, c] gives c of them. RandomHypergraph[{n, {e, a}}] and [{n, {{e1, a1}, ...}}] draw e_i hyperedges of arity a_i with vertices chosen with replacement from 1..n. Honors SeedRandom.

nodes.label: RandomImage
nodes.summary: RandomImage[] gives a 150x150 grey image of uniform noise on [0, 1]. RandomImage[max] scales the range to [0, max]; RandomImage[max, {w, h}] sets the size, and a single n means {n, n}. ColorSpace -> "RGB" gives three independent channels. Samples are drawn from the same stream as RandomReal, so SeedRandom makes the result reproducible.

nodes.label: RandomVariate
nodes.summary: RandomVariate[dist] draws one value from dist; RandomVariate[dist, n] draws a list of n. Supports NormalDistribution[mu, sigma] and UniformDistribution[{lo, hi}], each also usable with no arguments for the standard case. Draws come from the same stream as RandomReal, so SeedRandom makes them reproducible. A non-positive standard deviation, or an inverted range, returns unevaluated rather than producing NaNs.

nodes.label: RatCanonPrototype
nodes.summary: RatCanonPrototype[expr] (Phase-1 prototype) reduces a rational function over the differential/algebraic tower of expr via one FLINT reduction.

nodes.label: Re
nodes.summary: Re[z] gives the real part of numeric z; Re[Re[z]], Re[Im[z]], Re[Abs[z]], Re[Arg[z]] fold since those heads are real-valued.

nodes.label: ReIm
nodes.summary: ReIm[z] gives {Re[z], Im[z]}, the real and imaginary parts of numeric z as a list; real-valued arguments give {z, 0}.

nodes.label: RealDigits
nodes.summary: RealDigits[x] gives a list {digits, exp} of the digits in the approximate real number x together with the exponent such that the first digit is the coefficient of 10^(exp - 1).

nodes.label: RealExponent
nodes.summary: RealExponent[x] gives Log[10, |x|] -- the base-10 real exponent of x.

nodes.label: RegionCentroid
nodes.summary: RegionCentroid[Polygon[{{x1, y1}, ...}]] gives the centroid {cx, cy} of a simple 2D polygon with nonzero area. Exact coordinates give an exact result; Real coordinates give a machine-precision result.

nodes.label: RegionMember
nodes.summary: RegionMember[Polygon[{{x1, y1}, ...}], {x, y}] gives True if the point lies inside or on the boundary of the simple 2D polygon, and False otherwise.

nodes.label: RemoveAlphaChannel
nodes.summary: RemoveAlphaChannel[image] drops the alpha channel. RemoveAlphaChannel[image, b] instead COMPOSITES over a background of brightness b, which is the difference between forgetting the transparency and resolving it: a half-transparent white pixel over black is grey, where dropping alpha would leave it white.

nodes.label: Repeated
nodes.summary: p.. or Repeated[p] is a pattern object that represents a sequence of one or more expressions, each matching p.

nodes.label: RepeatedNull
nodes.summary: p... or RepeatedNull[p] is a pattern object that represents a sequence of zero or more expressions, each matching p.

nodes.label: RepeatedTiming
nodes.summary: RepeatedTiming[expr] evaluates expr repeatedly and returns a list of the average time in seconds used, together with the result obtained.

nodes.label: ReplaceList
nodes.summary: ReplaceList[expr, rules] attempts to transform the entire expression expr by applying a rule or list of rules in all possible ways, and returns a list of the results obtained.

nodes.label: Rest
nodes.summary: Rest[expr] gives all but the first element of expr.

nodes.label: Reverse
nodes.summary: Reverse[expr] reverses the order of elements in expr.

nodes.label: ReverseGraph
nodes.summary: ReverseGraph[g] reverses every directed edge of g; undirected edges, the edge order and the weights are kept.

nodes.label: RootMeanSquare
nodes.summary: RootMeanSquare[list] gives the root mean square of values in list.

nodes.label: RootReduce
nodes.summary: RootReduce[expr] canonicalises an algebraic expression: a constant algebraic number becomes a rational, a quadratic radical, or a Root object; a rational function over a radical tower has its denominator rationalised; a polynomial/rational function in a free variable has its constant-algebraic coefficients canonicalised. Threads over lists, rules (Solve results), equations, inequalities and logic. Option: Method -> "Automatic" | "Recursive" | "NumberField".

nodes.label: RotateLeft
nodes.summary: RotateLeft[expr, n] rotates the elements of expr n positions to the left.

nodes.label: RotateRight
nodes.summary: RotateRight[expr, n] rotates the elements of expr n positions to the right.

nodes.label: Row
nodes.summary: Row[{e1, e2, ...}] displays the ei concatenated together in a row.

nodes.label: SeriesData
nodes.summary: SeriesData[x, x0, {a0, a1, ...}, nmin, nmax, den]

nodes.label: SessionTime
nodes.summary: SessionTime[] gives the total number of seconds of wall-clock time elapsed since the beginning of the current Mathilda session.

nodes.label: SetAlphaChannel
nodes.summary: SetAlphaChannel[image] attaches a fully opaque alpha channel. SetAlphaChannel[image, a] sets one opacity everywhere when a is a number in [0, 1], or per pixel when a is an image of the same dimensions (read as grey, so a colour mask is not taken as its red channel alone). A mask of the wrong size is declined rather than resampled.

nodes.label: SetAttributes
nodes.summary: SetAttributes[s, attr] sets the attributes for s.

nodes.label: SetOptions
nodes.summary: SetOptions[s, name -> value, ...] sets default options for the symbol

nodes.label: Shortest
nodes.summary: Shortest[p] is a pattern object that matches the shortest sequence consistent with the pattern p.

nodes.label: Sign
nodes.summary: Sign[x] gives -1, 0, or 1 for real numeric x according to its sign, and z/Abs[z] for a nonzero numeric complex z.

nodes.label: SimpleGraphQ
nodes.summary: SimpleGraphQ[g] gives True if g is a graph with no self-loops or parallel edges -- every valid Mathilda graph -- and False otherwise.

nodes.label: Slot
nodes.summary: # or Slot[n] represents the n-th argument of a pure function. #name (Slot["name"], also #"str") is the value of key "name" in the association the function is applied to.

nodes.label: SlotSequence
nodes.summary: ## or SlotSequence[n] represents arguments from the n-th onward.

nodes.label: SmoothKernelDistribution
nodes.summary: SmoothKernelDistribution[data] gives a kernel density estimate as a LearnedDistribution, usable with PDF. The kernel is a product Gaussian with a per-dimension bandwidth from the multivariate normal-reference rule, which in one dimension is Silverman's 1.06 sigma n^(-1/5). SmoothKernelDistribution[data, h] sets the bandwidth explicitly, as one number or one per dimension. Being a normal-reference rule the default oversmooths strongly multimodal data -- a known property of the rule, and the reason the explicit form exists. A constant column has no scale and returns unevaluated.

nodes.label: Sort
nodes.summary: Sort[list] sorts the elements of list into canonical order.

nodes.label: Span
nodes.summary: i;;j represents a span of elements i through j. i;;j;;k represents a span in steps of k.

nodes.label: SquareFreeQ
nodes.summary: SquareFreeQ[expr] gives True if expr is a square-free number or polynomial -- no prime (or irreducible factor) occurs more than once, equivalently MoebiusMu[n] != 0 for an integer -- and False otherwise; the squarefree integers have density 6/Pi^2.

nodes.label: StandardDeviation
nodes.summary: StandardDeviation[data] gives the standard deviation estimate of the elements in data.

nodes.label: Standardize
nodes.summary: Standardize[data] shifts each column of data to zero mean and rescales it to unit sample standard deviation (divisor n-1, matching StandardDeviation). A flat list is treated as n observations of one variable. A constant column becomes exactly 0 rather than Indeterminate.

nodes.label: StarGraph
nodes.summary: StarGraph[n] gives the star on n vertices: the hub 1 joined to each of the n-1 leaves 2..n.

nodes.label: StreamPlot
nodes.summary: StreamPlot[{vx, vy}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts...]

nodes.label: StronglyConnectedComponents
nodes.summary: StronglyConnectedComponents[g] gives the strongly connected components of g (following edge directions).

nodes.label: Subgraph
nodes.summary: Subgraph[g, {v1, v2, ...}] gives the subgraph of g induced by the listed vertices (elements that are not vertices of g are ignored); Subgraph[g, patt] uses the vertices matching patt. Vertices come in the order given; edges in lower-triangular order of that vertex order. Edge weights are kept.

nodes.label: Subhypergraph
nodes.summary: Subhypergraph[h, {v1, ...}] gives the sub-hypergraph induced by the given vertices: those of them in h, and the hyperedges lying entirely among them.

nodes.label: SubresultantPolynomialRemainders
nodes.summary: SubresultantPolynomialRemainders[a, b, x] gives the polynomial-remainder

nodes.label: Subtract
nodes.summary: x - y or Subtract[x, y] represents x - y; rewritten by the evaluator

nodes.label: Sum
nodes.summary: Sum[f, {i, imax}] gives the sum of f for i from 1 to imax. Sum[f, {i, imin, imax}], Sum[f, {i, imin, imax, di}] and Sum[f, {i, {i1, i2, ...}}] use the standard iterator forms; multiple iterators give nested sums. Sum[f, i] gives the indefinite sum (antidifference). Symbolic and infinite sums are evaluated in closed form via Method -> "Polynomial" | "Geometric" | "Gosper".

nodes.label: Tally
nodes.summary: Tally[list] counts the number of occurrences of each distinct element in list.

nodes.label: Thinning
nodes.summary: Thinning[image] reduces the foreground to a one-pixel-wide skeleton by Zhang-Suen thinning, iterating until a pass deletes nothing. Thinning[image, n] stops after n iterations. The two subiterations are what preserve connectivity: deleting every individually-removable pixel in one pass severs a diagonal line, since two diagonal neighbours can each be removable while removing both disconnects the shape. A non-binary image is thresholded at 0.5 -- apply Binarize first for any other rule. The result is a "Bit" image, and it is always a subset of the input.

nodes.label: TimeUsed
nodes.summary: TimeUsed[] gives the total number of seconds of CPU time used so far in the current Mathilda session.

nodes.label: Times
nodes.summary: x * y * ... or Times[x, y, ...] represents a product of terms.

nodes.label: Timing
nodes.summary: Timing[expr] evaluates expr, and returns a list of the time in seconds used, together with the result obtained.

nodes.label: ToNDArray
nodes.summary: ToNDArray[list] returns list stored as a dense machine-precision buffer. The result is still a List -- same Head, same printed form, same elements -- but NDArrayQ gives True for it. ToNDArray[list, DataType -> "float64"] forces the element type. A mix of Integer and Real machine values is widened to a Real buffer (the integers become doubles); an all-Integer list stays Integer. Returns list unchanged when it is not rectangular, is empty, or holds any non-machine value. Unlike automatic packing it ignores the size threshold.

nodes.label: ToPackedArray
nodes.summary: ToPackedArray[list] is ToNDArray[list]: it returns list stored as a dense machine-precision buffer. The result is still a List -- same Head, same printed form, same elements -- but NDArrayQ gives True for it. Provided under Mathematica's name for the same operation; see ToNDArray.

nodes.label: ToeplitzMatrix
nodes.summary: ToeplitzMatrix[n] gives the n x n Toeplitz matrix with first row and column the integers 1..n.

nodes.label: Together
nodes.summary: Together[expr] combines fractions over a common denominator, then cancels.

nodes.label: TopologicalSort
nodes.summary: TopologicalSort[g] gives the vertices of the directed acyclic graph g ordered so that u precedes v for every edge u->v; ties go to the vertex earlier in VertexList[g]. TopologicalSort[{v->w, ...}] uses the rules as the graph. Left unevaluated if g has a cycle or an undirected edge.

nodes.label: TransversalHypergraph
nodes.summary: TransversalHypergraph[h] gives the hypergraph of all minimal transversals (minimal hitting sets) of h, on the vertices of h. For a plain List of hyperedges the List of minimal transversals is returned. Left unevaluated if the search exceeds its budget.

nodes.label: TreeGraphQ
nodes.summary: TreeGraphQ[g] gives True if g is a tree: at least one vertex, connected, and with no cycles, ignoring edge direction. A disconnected forest is not a tree.

nodes.label: TrueQ
nodes.summary: TrueQ[expr] yields True if expr is True, and False otherwise.

nodes.label: TuranGraph
nodes.summary: TuranGraph[n, k] gives the Turan graph: the complete k-partite graph on n vertices with parts as equal as possible.

nodes.label: UndirectedGraph
nodes.summary: UndirectedGraph[g] gives the undirected graph underlying g: u->v and v->u become the single edge u<->v, whose weight is the sum of theirs. Edges are oriented and ordered by VertexList position. An undirected g is returned unchanged.

nodes.label: UndirectedGraphQ
nodes.summary: UndirectedGraphQ[g] gives True if every edge of g is undirected (including when g has no edges), and False otherwise.

nodes.label: UniformDistribution
nodes.summary: UniformDistribution[{lo, hi}] represents a continuous uniform distribution; UniformDistribution[] is uniform on {0, 1}.

nodes.label: UniformHypergraphQ
nodes.summary: UniformHypergraphQ[h] gives True if every hyperedge of h has the same arity. UniformHypergraphQ[h, k] gives True if h is k-uniform.

nodes.label: Unique
nodes.summary: Unique[] generates a new symbol; Unique["x"] or Unique[x] uses a name prefix; Unique[{x, ...}] gives a list of fresh symbols. Each is Temporary and never previously used.

nodes.label: VandermondeMatrix
nodes.summary: VandermondeMatrix[{x1, ..., xn}] gives the n x n Vandermonde matrix with entry (i, j) equal to xi^(j-1).

nodes.label: Variance
nodes.summary: Variance[data] gives the unbiased variance estimate of the elements in data.

nodes.label: VectorPlot
nodes.summary: VectorPlot[{vx, vy}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts...]

nodes.label: Verbatim
nodes.summary: Verbatim[expr] is a pattern object that matches expr taken literally: the pattern constructs inside expr (Blank, Pattern, ...) are not interpreted, so Verbatim[x_] matches only the literal expression x_.

nodes.label: VerifySolutions
nodes.summary: VerifySolutions is an option for Solve.  With VerifySolutions ->

nodes.label: VertexAdd
nodes.summary: VertexAdd[g, v] adds the vertex v to the graph g; VertexAdd[g, {v1, v2, ...}] adds several. Vertices already present are ignored; new ones are appended in order. Edge weights are kept.

nodes.label: VertexConnectivity
nodes.summary: VertexConnectivity[g] gives the minimum number of vertices whose removal disconnects g.

nodes.label: VertexCount
nodes.summary: VertexCount[g] gives the number of vertices in the graph g.

nodes.label: VertexCoverQ
nodes.summary: VertexCoverQ[g, vlist] gives True if every edge of g has an endpoint in vlist.

nodes.label: VertexDegree
nodes.summary: VertexDegree[g] gives the list of vertex degrees; VertexDegree[g,v] gives the degree of vertex v.

nodes.label: VertexDelete
nodes.summary: VertexDelete[g, v] removes the vertex v and its incident edges from g; VertexDelete[g, {v1, ...}] removes several (each must be a vertex of g, else the call stays unevaluated); VertexDelete[g, patt] removes every vertex matching patt. Vertex and edge order and edge weights are kept.

nodes.label: VertexEccentricity
nodes.summary: VertexEccentricity[g, v] gives the largest distance from v to any vertex reachable from v. With EdgeWeight the weights are lengths and, as in Wolfram, a vertex v cannot reach makes it Infinity.

nodes.label: VertexInDegree
nodes.summary: VertexInDegree[g] / VertexInDegree[g,v] gives in-degrees (incoming directed edges; undirected edges count for both).

nodes.label: VertexIndex
nodes.summary: VertexIndex[g, v] gives the position of the vertex v in VertexList[g]; VertexIndex[g, {v1, ...}] gives a list of positions.

nodes.label: VertexList
nodes.summary: VertexList[g] gives the list of vertices of the graph g.

nodes.label: VertexOutDegree
nodes.summary: VertexOutDegree[g] / VertexOutDegree[g,v] gives out-degrees (outgoing directed edges; undirected edges count for both).

nodes.label: VertexQ
nodes.summary: VertexQ[g, v] gives True if v is a vertex of the graph g (compared structurally, as by SameQ), and False otherwise.

nodes.label: VertexReplace
nodes.summary: VertexReplace[g, {v1 -> w1, ...}] replaces vertices of g according to the rules (applied to each vertex as by Replace, so patterns work). Vertices mapped together merge; a merge that would create a self-loop or a parallel edge leaves the call unevaluated. Edge weights are kept.

nodes.label: WeaklyConnectedComponents
nodes.summary: WeaklyConnectedComponents[g] gives the weakly connected components of g.

nodes.label: WeightedAdjacencyMatrix
nodes.summary: WeightedAdjacencyMatrix[g] gives the adjacency matrix of g with each entry the corresponding edge's weight (0 where there is no edge). Equal to AdjacencyMatrix[g] when g has no EdgeWeight.

nodes.label: WeightedGraphQ
nodes.summary: WeightedGraphQ[g] gives True if g carries edge weights (EdgeWeight).

nodes.label: WheelGraph
nodes.summary: WheelGraph[n] gives the wheel graph with n vertices: vertex 1 joined to every vertex of the cycle 2, ..., n.

nodes.label: While
nodes.summary: While[test, body] evaluates test, then body, repeatedly, until test first fails to give True.

nodes.label: With
nodes.summary: With[{x = x0, ...}, expr] specifies that x should be replaced by x0 throughout expr.
